intro: Searching for a dilapidations surveyor near me usually means you're facing the end of a commercial lease and need to understand your repair obligations or challenge a claim. Whether you're a tenant worried about a large schedule of dilapidations or a landlord wanting to enforce lease terms, you need someone who knows this specialist area. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK surveyor who can assess your situation and quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a dilapidations surveyor usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a dilapidations surveyor are dealing with a commercial lease ending and need expert help to navigate repair obligations and negotiations.
needs: You're a tenant who has received a schedule of dilapidations from your landlord and need to check whether the claimed works are actually required under the lease.
You're a landlord wanting to prepare a proper claim for dilapidations at the end of a tenancy and need a surveyor to assess the property and quantify the loss.
You're unsure whether a schedule of condition from the start of the lease protects you from certain repairs now, and you need advice on how it affects your position.
You want to negotiate a settlement with the other side but need a professional to go through the claim and advise on a fair figure before you respond.
You're facing a dilapidations claim and want to understand the pre-action protocol so you can respond correctly and avoid unnecessary escalation.
context: Dilapidations claims in the UK often follow a pre-action protocol, which sets out steps the parties should take before going to court. This can include exchanging information and considering negotiation or mediation. A surveyor can help you navigate these steps and assess the merits of the claim.

Many surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance and offer a complaints process. Chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS. When choosing a surveyor, check the RICS directory and ask about their experience with dilapidations.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Whether you are the landlord or the tenant, as this affects the type of advice you need.
The type of property and its approximate size, such as office, retail or industrial, to help match you with a surveyor experienced in that sector.
Whether a schedule of condition exists from the start of the lease, as this can limit your repair liabilities.
The stage you are at: whether you have received a schedule of dilapidations, are preparing one, or are already in negotiation.
Any deadlines you are aware of, such as the lease end date or a date by which you need to respond to a claim.
Your location, so iComply can introduce you to a surveyor who covers your area.
questions: Are you a member of RICS, and is your firm regulated by RICS?
What experience do you have with dilapidations claims for properties like mine?
What report or advice will you provide, and will it cover both liability and likely costs?
How do you approach negotiation with the other side, and do you offer representation if needed?
What information do you need from me to get started, and what are your fees?
Can you explain how the pre-action protocol applies to my situation?

faqs.a: A dilapidations surveyor is a surveyor who specialises in advising landlords and tenants on repair obligations at the end of a lease and negotiating claims. They can assess the property, interpret the lease terms and help you understand your position.

faqs.q: Do I need a dilapidations surveyor if I'm a tenant?
faqs.a: If you've received a schedule of dilapidations or are approaching the end of your lease, a surveyor can help you check whether the claimed works are reasonable and negotiate a settlement. They can also advise on the effect of any schedule of condition.

faqs.q: What should I do if I disagree with a dilapidations claim?
faqs.a: You should seek professional advice from a dilapidations surveyor who can assess the claim and advise on your options. They can help you negotiate or respond within the pre-action protocol.
